findings.finding: ONNX Runtime exposes execution providers behind a common inference session interface.
findings.opportunity_or_risk: Report provider registration without claiming every node is accelerated.
findings.engineering_cost: small adapter with provider checks and integration tests
findings.verification_needed: CPU integration now; physical accelerator tests later

findings.finding: ExecuTorch loads exported PTE programs and invokes methods through its Python runtime; exports are target-specific.
findings.relevance: PyTorch export and on-device inference path
findings.opportunity_or_risk: Do not imply that one compiled model runs on every accelerator.
findings.roadmap_delta: none; pre-exported PTE is the initial boundary
findings.verification_needed: real Linux PTE export and execution; target device measurements deferred

findings.finding: Dynamic quantization is available through ONNX Runtime, but speed and numerical effects depend on model and hardware.
findings.direction_alignment: supports measured optimization rather than assumed improvement
findings.opportunity_or_risk: Retain the source hash and compare quantized outputs with golden vectors.
findings.engineering_cost: bounded transformation and numerical regression tests
findings.roadmap_delta: none; dynamic INT8 first, static calibration deferred
findings.verification_needed: quantized MatMul fixture and tolerance-failure tests

overall_recommendation: Implement the requested toolkit with existing runtimes, immutable artifacts, and transport-independent contracts.
evidence_gaps: No claim about ExecuTorch organizational migration is needed
authority: Advisory research only; initial implementation is authorized by the MVP request.
